extraFields.label: Council tax
extraFields.help: Your monthly council tax bill. Most councils bill in 10 instalments; spread it over 12 months here. Living alone usually gets 25% off.

single.note: Band A–C bill with the 25% single-person discount; England average Band D is £2,392 a year (£199 a month) in 2026-27. Estimate by band.

suburban.note: Band C–E bill; England average Band D £2,392 a year in 2026-27 (gov.uk). Estimate by band.

youngpro.note: Band B–D bill, no discount for a couple; England average Band D £2,392 a year in 2026-27. Estimate by band.

extraFields.label: TV licence
extraFields.help: Needed to watch live TV or use BBC iPlayer. £180 a year from April 2026, about £15 a month.

localTips.title: Check for a fixed energy deal below the price cap
localTips.why: Most homes on a standard variable tariff pay the Ofgem price cap rate. Fixed deals and smart time-of-use tariffs are sometimes cheaper.
tips: Compare fixed tariffs against the current price cap on a comparison site before the next cap change (January, April, July, October).
Give a meter reading and switch to paying by Direct Debit, which is cheaper than paying on receipt of bill.
If you have a smart meter and can shift usage, look at time-of-use tariffs with cheaper overnight rates.

pct.note: Assumed saving versus the price cap; depends on deals available at the time.

localTips.title: Claim council tax discounts you are entitled to
localTips.why: If only one adult lives in a home, the bill is 25% lower, and some bands are wrong.
tips: If you live alone (or the only other adults are students or apprentices), apply for the 25% single person discount on your council’s website.
Check your band against similar homes on your street on the Valuation Office Agency (or Scottish Assessors) site.
Ask your council about Council Tax Reduction if your income is low.

pct.note: Single person discount is 25%; only applies to people living alone.
